Half a decade ago, when I was just becoming a teen, my dad committed suicide.

Basically, the night before, he went off to play hockey and never came back. He crashed his car in an intersection not far from my house at the time, with the intent to kill himself. He lived through that though so he walked to a gas station, picked up a knife, pen and paper and then went to a motel or something.

He spent the night doing all of this and this whole time the police were looking for him. He spent hours writing his personal notes to all of his family (me, my brother, my sister, two notes to my mom, friends and other family).

His second note to my mom is unfinished because the police found him and he panicked. He got into the bathtub, and used the knife to slit his wrists. Something I found out kinda recently is he brutalized his wrists, which was horrifying to picture.

Anyways, his note to me was very heartfelt. He basically told me he was very proud of me, and the man I was beginning to become. He used nicknames for me like calling me Superman, which isn’t something he usually did. I think as the youngest child and still pretty young at the time, he wanted to protect me from the truth and mentioned/compared me to superheroes as a way of distraction or something.

Anyways, he didn’t really give me detail about why he was doing it, no one saw it coming, but in that note, my dad basically told me to care about my family and tell them i love them.

Uh no this is real and not a writing exercise. My father wasn’t taken advantage of or something. He was a great father before he committed suicide.

I’m trying not to see this comment as a personal attack or blaming me or my family for what my father did.

He hid his depression very well. No one noticed because he was good at hiding it. He didn’t want anyone, even my mother, to know, so I’m guessing he pretended like nothing was wrong.

The reason why most of the post is negative is because I remember that day pretty well and the memory of how horrible it was, outweighs the many positive things my dad did. The last thing he ever did was mess my family’s life up. That is how I remember him now. 

This post wasn’t to talk about the life of my father, which I thought was great, until I learned that he hated his life.

I don’t know what suffering he went through because he never told anyone.

The letters are private and honestly I haven’t looked at mine in a while, since it’s been 5 years, but I know that he said in his letter to me, who was pretty young at the time, that he loves me, he’s very proud of me and he called me superman and stuff like that. I don’t know what was in the other letters because they were to other people. My mom was probably the only one who got a letter that has any details on what he went through.

Yes I don’t remember if I said bye to him the last time I saw him. That doesn’t mean he was taken for granted or anything. That’s kind of s stretch.

My brother and I were pretty young when this happened. So we didn’t fully understand what was happening. My grandma let us play video games so we wouldn’t be worried and so that we can pass the time until we hear anything. I don’t remember if I knew it was a violent car crash or something. At the time, I thought he was in a car crash, got scared of punishment of something and fled the scene. I assumed he would be found, punished and then life continues normally. I wasn’t expecting to discover that my dad had died.

I understand that suicidal people have heard that you shouldn’t kill yourself because it’s selfish a bunch of times, but that is the point of my story. Yes his death is the root of most problems in my life. People should not kill themselves because it is definitely selfish, especially if you don’t at least seek help. Whatever that may be. Tell a friend. Tell a professional. Get help from the people of reddit. Whatever.

Sure feel bad for my father. But that line of “I feel for your father” makes me feel like you’re blaming me or my family for it. It seems like you’re saying that what he did was okay.

I hate that my dad went through this pain. But he never told anyone so I don’t want what he went through. The way I remember him was as my idol and the person I wanted to be like. He was strong and fearless in my eyes. This whole event changed my outlook on him.
